gaps.sentence: We ___ a visit to the museum while we were in Vienna.
gaps.explanation: pay a visit to somebody/something means to go and see them briefly.

gaps.sentence: Halfway through the film, the children were fast ___.
gaps.explanation: fast asleep means completely asleep; it is the fixed collocation with 'fast'.

gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the blame for the accident onto the weather.
gaps.explanation: 'Shift the blame onto somebody' = transfer responsibility.

gaps.sentence: All candidates must ___ the written exam in June.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'exam' from the candidate's side
gaps.explanation: take an exam (or sit an exam) means to be tested; 'give an exam' is not used in British English.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.
